nahhas-irab:1-3.t: وَالْمُرْسَلاتِ عُرْفاً (1): Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned views on these verses, and we will add explanation and clarification. It was read before Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥafṣ, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Abū al-ʿUbaydayn, from Ibn Masʿūd, on the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: وَالْمُرْسَلاتِ عُرْفاً (1) — he said: the winds. فَالْعاصِفاتِ عَصْفاً (2) — he said: the wind. وَالنَّاشِراتِ نَشْراً (3) — he said: the wind. Abū Jaʿfar said: it has also been related from Ibn Masʿūd that he said: الْمُرْسَلاتِ are the angels. The view that they are the winds is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Ṣāliḥ, Mujāhid and Qatāda. And فَالْعاصِفاتِ are the winds — that is from three of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them. وَالنَّاشِراتِ: it has been related from Ibn Masʿūd that they are the angels; the first report, that it is the wind, is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās; and from Abū Ṣāliḥ that النَّاشِراتِ is the rain.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: From Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās: they are the angels. Saʿīd related from Qatāda: فَالْفارِقاتِ فَرْقاً — he said: the Qur'an, which distinguishes between truth and falsehood; and the construction on this view is: "by the distinguishing verses".

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
From Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās; they said: the angels. Qatāda said: the angels who deliver the Reminder to the prophets, peace be upon them. And from Abū Ṣāliḥ about some of these: he said: the prophets. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned that the adjective here has been put in place of the noun qualified, and for this reason the disagreement arose. If the construction is:
"by the Lord of the المرسلات", then the meaning is one, and the oath is by Allah, Mighty and Majestic. If we explain this further, we say: we have mentioned what has been said — that they are the winds, that they are the angels, and that they are the messengers, peace be upon them — and we have found no decisive proof that rules in favour of one of these views; so it must be referred back to the generality of the apparent meaning, and it is general for all of these things. عُرْفاً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) if its meaning is "following one another"; and if its meaning is "and the angels sent with العرف", i.e. with Allah's command, obedience to Him and His books, then the construction is بالعرف, the bāʾ being dropped so the verb became transitive, as Sībawayh recited: [al-Basīṭ] 516-
أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به ... فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب
(I have commanded you [to do] good, so do what you were commanded, for I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)
عَصْفاً, نَشْراً and فَرْقاً are maṣdars (verbal nouns) conveying emphasis. فَالْمُلْقِياتِ ذِكْراً: [ذِكْراً is] a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
«[Translator's note: the first reading being described (عُذْراً أَوْ نُذْراً, with sukūn on both dhāls) has dropped out of the beginning of the entry.]» [This is] the reading of Abū ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. The people of the two Sanctuaries, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read عُذْراً with a sukūn on the dhāl and «أو نذرا» with ḍamma on the dhāl. It is related from Zayd ibn Thābit and al-Ḥasan: «عذرا أو نذرا» with ḍamma on both dhāls. Giving both a sukūn is on the basis that they are both maṣdars (verbal nouns), as you say شكرته شكرا; and it may be that the original in both is the ḍamma, which was dropped because it was found heavy. Giving both ḍamma is on the basis that they are the plurals of عذير and نذير; and they may [also] be maṣdars, like شغلته شغلا. And عذير has the meaning of إعذار (excuse), as [the poet] said: [al-Wāfir] 517-
أريد حباءه ويريد قتلي ... عذيرك من خليلك من مراد
(I want to gift him, and he wants to kill me — who will excuse you for your friend from Murād?)
i.e. your excuse; and as [another] said: [al-Hazaj] 518-
نذير الحيّ من عدوان ... كانوا حيّة الأرض
(The warning of the tribe of ʿAdwān: they were the serpent of the land.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: these two verses are recited thus, in the accusative. Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 519-
عذيرك من مولى إذا نمت لم ينم ... يقول الخنا أو تعتريك زنابره
(Who will excuse you for a kinsman who, when you sleep, does not sleep, speaking obscenity, or his stings assail you?)
i.e. your excuse for this.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: I.e. of the resurrection, the reckoning and the requital. This is the apodosis (jawāb) of the oath. «ما» here means "that which" (الذي), written separately from «إنّ»; and it may not here be a separating [particle] with «لا» «[Translator's note: so in the source; perhaps «ما» meant as redundant/cancelling.]» redundant — do you not see that in its khabar (predicate) there is the lām confirming the khabar of إنّ? The hāʾ [the object pronoun] was dropped because of the length of the noun; the construction is: "that which you are promised — of the reckoning, the reward and the punishment — will surely occur".

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
النجوم was put in the nominative by an implied verb like this one [i.e. طُمِسَتْ], because إذا here has the status of the particles of conditional requital. If someone says: Sībawayh said about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ [al-Rūm: 36], that «إذا» is an apodosis with the status of the fāʾ, and it only became an apodosis with the status of the fāʾ because one does not begin with it, just as one does not begin with the fāʾ; yet one has begun with it here, and you say إذا قمت قمت, beginning [with it]. Abū Jaʿfar said: I do not know of anyone who has faulted Sībawayh in this. The argument for him is that «إذا», when it is for surprise (mufājaʾa), one does not begin with it, as in His saying إِذا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ; and when it has the meaning of conditional requital, one begins with it. But Sībawayh has been opposed «[Translator's note: the source has «عوض», apparently «عورض».]» on the grounds that the fāʾ can enter upon it, so how can it be a substitute for it?
The answer is that it only enters [upon it] for emphasis. And the apodosis of فَإِذَا النُّجُومُ طُمِسَتْ is وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ; it has been said that the fāʾ is omitted; and it has been said that the apodosis is omitted.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read وَإِذَا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ ] with hamza and a doubled qāf. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar the grammarian and Khālid ibn Ilyās read أُقِّتَتْ «[Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; the reading described is أُقِتَتْ.]» with hamza and a light qāf. Abū ʿAmr read «وقّتت» with wāw and a doubled qāf, and al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar read «وقتت» with wāw and a light qāf. Abū Jaʿfar said: the original in it is the wāw, because it is derived from الوقت (time); [Allah,] Mighty and Majestic, said: كانَتْ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتاباً مَوْقُوتاً [al-Nisāʾ: 103] — this is from وقتت with a light [qāf]. But the ḍamma is found heavy on the wāw, so it is replaced by hamza. Sībawayh mentioned the two forms وقّتت and أقّتت without putting one before the other; so since both are eloquent, the more appropriate is to follow the written text.

nahhas-irab:12-13.t: لِيَوْمِ الْفَصْلِ: it has been said: the verb to which the lām is attached has been omitted, and the full stop is at لأي يوم أجّلت; then a verb was implied: "it was deferred to the Day of Decision". And it has been said: ليوم الفصل is a badal (substitute), with the lām repeated, like لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفاً مِنْ فِضَّةٍ [al-Zukhruf: 33] «[Translator's note: reference added by the translator.]». And it has been said: the lām means إلى ("to").

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: The first and second «ما» are in the position of rafʿ (nominative) as a mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: I.e. those who deny the Day of Resurrection and what is in it.

nahhas-irab:16-17.t: Al-Aʿraj read أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ الْأَوَّلِينَ ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ الْآخِرِينَ, putting نُتْبِعُهُمُ in the jussive «[Translator's note: i.e. نُتْبِعْهُمُ; the source prints the standard vowels.]», because it is conjoined to نهلك. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a solecism; and Abū Ḥātim said: this is a solecism; and Ismāʿīl mentioned that it is not permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: «ثم» is one of the conjunctions, and [the question] concerns only the meaning; and in meaning it is not impossible, because it has been said about the meaning of أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ الْأَوَّلِينَ that they are the people of Nūḥ, ʿĀd and Thamūd, and that the later ones are the people of Ibrāhīm ﷺ, the people of Madyan and Pharaoh. Abū Jaʿfar said: on this basis the reading with the jussive is sound.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: I.e. thus is My way with whoever persists in crime: that I destroy him for his crime.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: I.e. to whoever denies what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has informed, and His power over whatever He wills.

nahhas-irab:20-23.t:
Assimilating the qāf into the kāf [in نَخْلُقْكُمْ] is permissible. From Ibn ʿAbbās: «مهين» means weak. Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read فَقَدَرْنا light, and Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read فَقَدَرْنا doubled «[Translator's note: i.e. فَقَدَّرْنا; the source prints the same vowels for both.]». The light form is more likely, because after it comes فَنِعْمَ الْقادِرُونَ and not المقدّرون; yet the reading with doubling is good, because it has been reported that they are two forms with one meaning: one says قدر and قدّره; and He said: نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنا بَيْنَكُمُ الْمَوْتَ [al-Wāqiʿa: 60]. It is not objectionable for two forms with one meaning to come in one place; He said: فَمَهِّلِ الْكافِرِينَ أَمْهِلْهُمْ رُوَيْداً [al-Ṭāriq: 17]. And the poet said: [al-Basīṭ] 520-
وأنكرتني وما كان الذي نكرت ... من الحوادث إلّا الشّيب والصّلعا
(She did not recognise me, and what she failed to recognise of the vicissitudes was nothing but grey hair and baldness.)
It has been said: the meaning of فقدرنا is [We determined] the drop, the clot and the lump of flesh. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: فقدرنا means "We had power over [it]".
فَنِعْمَ الْقادِرُونَ: [الْقادِرُونَ is] nominative by نعم, and the construction is: "how excellent are the determiners — We".

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: [Woe to the deniers] of the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, over these things and others.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: One says كفته when he gathers it and secures it; so the earth gathers people on its surface alive and in its belly dead. The derivation of this is from الكفتة, which is the container of a thing; and likewise الكفتة «[Translator's note: the source repeats the same word; the variant vowelling meant has been lost.]».

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: [أَحْياءً is] accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "We gather them in this state"; and it may be accusative because the action falls on it, i.e. "it gathers the living and the dead".

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: وَجَعَلْنا فِيها رَواسِيَ شامِخاتٍ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: He says: lofty mountains. He said: وماءً فُراتاً: fresh. And ʿIkrima related from him: «ماء فراتا» means Sayḥān, Jayḥān, the Euphrates and the Nile; he said: and all fresh water in the world is from these four rivers.

nahhas-irab:28-29.t: انْطَلِقُوا إِلى ما كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ (29), i.e. it will be said to them. Yaʿqūb al-Ḥaḍramī claimed that one of the readers read «انطلقوا» with fatḥa on the lām, as a past verb; as for the first, there was no disagreement about it.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: لا ظَلِيلٍ is a naʿt (adjective) of ظلّ, i.e. not shading from the heat, and it does not protect from the flame of the Fire.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t:
إِنَّها تَرْمِي بِشَرَرٍ: [شَرَر is] the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, as [the poet] said: [al-Wāfir] 521-
وتوقد ناركم شررا ويرفع ... لكم في كلّ مجمعة لواء
(Your fire is kindled into sparks, and a banner is raised for you at every gathering.)
and the dialect of Banū Tamīm is شرار. كَالْقَصْرِ is read in three ways «[Translator's note: the source prints the same vowels throughout; the readings meant are القَصْر, القَصَر and القِصَر.]»: the reading of the generality is كَالْقَصْرِ; from Ibn ʿAbbās and a group of his companions: كَالْقَصْرِ with fatḥa on the ṣād; and from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr there are two reports, in one of them كَالْقَصْرِ and in the other كَالْقَصْرِ. As was read before Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq: Naṣr ibn ʿAlī said: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us: Yūnus narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan: إنها ترمي بشرر كَالْقَصْرِ with kasra on the qāf. Naṣr said: and my father narrated to us: Yūnus narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan: بِشَرَرٍ كَالْقَصْرِ — he said: the stumps of palm trees. Abū Jaʿfar said: القصر with fatḥa on the qāf and sukūn on the ṣād — there are two views on its meaning. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: كَالْقَصْرِ — he said: He says: like the great palace. And likewise Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: it is a palace among palaces. Abū ʿUbayd said, from Ḥajjāj, from Hārūn; he said: القصر is thick firewood, like جمرة and جمر, and تمرة and تمر. Abū Jaʿfar said: sounder than this from al-Ḥasan is what was read before Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Ismāʿīl, from Naṣr; he said: Yazīd narrated to us: Yūnus narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan; he said: «كالقصر» is the singular of القصور (palaces). Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a clear view; and the Arabs liken the she-camel and the camel to a palace, as [the poet] said: [al-Basīṭ] 522-
كأنها برج روميّ يشيّده ... بان بجصّ وآجرّ وأحجار
(As if she were a Byzantine tower, raised high by a builder with gypsum, baked bricks and stones.)
As for القصر [with fatḥa on the ṣād], Mujāhid and Qatāda said: it is the stumps of palm trees. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: القصر is the piece of timber three cubits long or more or less. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the soundest thing said about it; and from it the fuller is called قصّار, because he works with timber like this. القصر in this sense is the plural of قصرة — and حاجة / حوج has been heard from the Arabs — and it may be the plural of قصرة, as حلقة / حلق has been heard. Someone said: الشرر is a plural and القصر a singular, so how could it be likened to it?
The answer is that it may be a singular that indicates a plural, or the plural of قصرة, or the act is meant, i.e. "like the great size of the palace". Al-Farrāʾ argued that it is preferable to read «كالقصر» with sukūn on the ṣād, because the verses are [rhymed] on this; do you not see that after it comes «صفر»? And he argued from the readers' reading of يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدَّاعِ إِلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ [al-Qamar: 6] with ḍamma on the kāf, because the verses are so, while in another place: فَحاسَبْناها حِساباً شَدِيداً وَعَذَّبْناها عَذاباً نُكْراً [al-Ṭalāq: 8] with sukūn on the kāf. He said: the readers agreed on giving a vowel to the first and a sukūn to the second. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is an ugly mistake: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr read يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدَّاعِ إِلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ
with sukūn on the kāf «[Translator's note: the source prints نُكُرٍ with ḍamma; the reading described is نُكْرٍ.]». And what he brought regarding the agreement of verse-endings does not hold consistently and cannot be applied by analogy.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: «[Translator's note: the first reading described (جِمالَتٌ) has dropped out of the beginning of the entry.]» [This is] the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash ibn ʿĪsā «[Translator's note: so in the source («الأعمش بن عيسى»), apparently a corruption.]», Ṭalḥa, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «كأنه جماله صفر» «[Translator's note: i.e. جِمالَةٌ.]»; and from Ibn ʿAbbās: «جمالات صفر» with ḍamma on the jīm. The first reading would be the plural of جمال or of جمالة; and جمالة is the plural of جمل, like حجر / حجارة. And جمالات may have the meaning of جمال, as one says رخل / رخال and ظئر / ظؤار; the tāʾ is for the feminine of the group. However, the exegetes say: they [جُمالات] are the ropes of ships — among them Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr — except that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: pieces of copper. And it may be derived from الشيء المجمل (the thing gathered together).

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
[هذا يَوْمُ لا يَنْطِقُونَ is] a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the readers agreed on the nominative of يوم. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is close to what preceded. It is related from al-Aʿraj and al-Aʿmash that they read هذا يَوْمُ لا يَنْطِقُونَ in the accusative «[Translator's note: i.e. يَوْمَ; the source prints the nominative vowel.]». There are two views on its accusative. One is that it is an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "this that we have mentioned is on this day". The other view, mentioned by al-Farrāʾ, is that «يوم» is indeclinable (mabnī). This is wrong according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh: in their view adverbs are not made indeclinable with the imperfect verb, because it is inflected; they are only made indeclinable with the past, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 523- على حين عاتبت المشيب على الصّبا (At the time when I reproached grey hair for [the loss of] youth.)

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: [فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ is] conjoined; and al-Farrāʾ claimed that the nominative was chosen in it so that the verse-endings agree.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: [هذا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ is] a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). جَمَعْناكُمْ وَالْأَوَّلِينَ: [الْأَوَّلِينَ is] conjoined (nasaq) to the kāf and mīm.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: The yāʾ [of فَكِيدُونِ] was dropped because the nūn became a compensation for it, since it has kasra, and it is at the end of a verse.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: Whoever gives kasra to the ʿayn [in عِيُونٍ] dislikes the ḍamma together with the yāʾ.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: The original is يشتهونه; the hāʾ, the noun [i.e. the pronoun], was dropped.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: I.e. this will be said to them.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: The kāf is in the position of naṣb (accusative), i.e. "a requital like that".

nahhas-irab:45-46.t: كُلُوا وَتَمَتَّعُوا قَلِيلًا is connected to what follows it «[Translator's note: so in the source («بما يليه»); in the sequence it relates to what precedes, verse 45.]», i.e. it was said to the deniers: كُلُوا وَتَمَتَّعُوا قَلِيلًا, i.e. for a short time and a little enjoyment.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: [i.e.] and when they are told: "Pray". Others said: bowing was the hardest of things for the Arabs, to the point that some of them embraced Islam and refused to bow.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: The bāʾ occurred before أي, even though the interrogative has the front of the sentence, because the prepositions with what follows them have the status of a single thing. Do you not see that your saying نظرت إلى زيد and نظرت زيدا have the same meaning?
